draft.emotion: hurried and apologetic, rushing out the door
notes: Common in 'più tardi' (later, e.g. 'a più tardi', see you later) and 'fare tardi' (to be running late / to stay out late).
Do not confuse with the noun 'ritardo' (delay), used in 'essere in ritardo' (to be late for an appointment or schedule).
